title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is a case of synthetic media used to put words into a real person's mouth. The videos depicted a named candidate stating things she did not say, and they were published to a public platform by a sitting officeholder's campaign during an active election. The failure is not a model error in the ordinary sense, because the false statements were the intended output, not an accident of training or inference.

The point of deployment is the campaign's own communications channel, where generated video was posted as if it were authentic speech by an opponent. Nothing in the reporting describes any check between generation and publication, and no platform or campaign mechanism is said to have flagged or removed the clips. Catching this would have required either the producing campaign to label the material as synthetic or the platform to detect and mark it, and neither is reported to have happened.

What is not established is whether the videos were made with any particular tool, whether any court has found defamation, or whether the cease-and-desist letter has any legal effect. A letter is a demand, not a ruling, and the campaign's dismissal of it is a statement of position rather than a finding of fact.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over his use of AI deepfake videos. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. Van Orden posted videos to X showing fake versions of Cooke saying things she never said, including a clip shared Aug. 4. The letter, dated Sept. 30, says Cooke never made those statements and warns Van Orden could face defamation claims under state law.

Van Orden's campaign dismissed the letter as a tantrum. Cooke's attorneys say they are monitoring his social media accounts and weighing all legal options if he continues. Van Orden responded this week by posting another AI-assisted video featuring a duck saying "Cease and desist!" Cooke previously lost to Van Orden in 2024 by about 3 percentage points.
